phrases.latin: Baucis ignem excitat et flat, dōnec ex fūmō flamma oritur
phrases.english: Baucis stirs up the fire and blows until a flame rises from the smoke
It’s cold; I’ll light the stove.

phrases.latin: vīlla recēpisset lacrimōsō nōn sine fūmō, ūdōs cum foliīs rāmōs ūrente camīnō
phrases.english: (if) a country house had not taken us in, not without smoke that made our eyes water, as the stove burned damp branches, leaves and all

sources: Lewis & Short: caminus · Lewis & Short: excito
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 120.
